why: Stops checking that Exit PRESERVED everything that was not a developer parameter. #238 requires it, and the natural wrong implementation -- rebuilding the query from scratch with only the parameters you recognise -- passes every "is dev gone" assertion while silently breaking a deep link or a router's own parameters. This is the half of the contract that fails quietly.
killedBy: exitContractFailures: judging where Exit landed FAILS when an unrelated parameter is dropped
exitContractFailures: judging where Exit landed FAILS when an unrelated parameter is altered rather than dropped
